The route actually taken is the deviation the rider describes: the trace leaves the recommended PIE line at the Clementi Avenue 6 exit at 08:42:55, runs down Clementi Avenue 6 and Commonwealth Avenue West, and rejoins at Holland Road / Commonwealth Avenue West at 08:53:16 — the route was changed and the rider's account of it is correct. Catchment not in dispute. (POL-RD-22 uses the trace to show which route was taken and when, not to re-measure distance.)

The driver never informed the rider of the deviation, before it or at the point of it, as POL-RD-21 requires. The trip record's own derived block for POL-RD-21 shows messages_during_trip as an empty list, and in_app_calls is empty too, so there is neither an in-app chat notice nor a recorded verbal one. The deviation occurred at 08:42:55; the chat log contains nothing after 08:36:12.

The rider's single message ("Ok", 08:36:12) cannot be an acknowledgment of the deviation. It replies to the driver's 08:35:52 message about where the car was parked at Westgate, and it was sent six minutes before the deviation at 08:42:55 and before the trip even started at 08:37:22. There is no agreed deviation on this record, so POL-RD-24(a) is not in play.

The driver's own statement in this dispute concedes the notification failure: "Forgot to inform, sorry." Under POL-RD-21 a verbal notice with no recording in the record cannot be established (POL-GEN-26), and in any event the driver does not assert he gave one — he says he forgot. The notification limb fails on the driver's own account as well as on the chat log.

The rider does not need the traffic question resolved in his favour, because it does not change the money. If the LTA advisory is read as justifying the reroute, the driver still failed to inform, which is POL-RD-24(b) — refund of the excess distance fare. If the advisory is not read as intersecting the recommended route, the case is POL-RD-24(d) — refund of the excess distance fare in full. Both rows pay the same figure; the rider's entitlement follows on either reading, and the rider presses the refund row rather than asking the tribunal to resolve the traffic question.

On the traffic limb specifically, POL-RD-23 requires a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY that intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window, and the artifact's own derived fields leave intersects_route undetermined (value null, determined_by judge). The rider's submission is that the justification is not established on the artifact as presented, so POL-RD-24(d) is the row the record best fits — but the rider's claim stands on row (b) as well if the judge finds otherwise.

The amount owed is fixed by POL-RD-24's excess-distance formula from the clean ledger: deviation_km 1.40 times per_km_rate_sgd 0.72, with no surge, equals 1.008 SGD, rounded to the cent as 1.01 SGD. The fare breakdown confirms the charge was metered, no surge applied and payment status CHARGED, so the money is still with the driver's side and is recoverable.

The rider asked for 4.00 SGD; the policy's measure is narrower, and the rider presses his claim to 1.01 SGD and no further. The correct outcome is therefore PARTIAL_REFUND of 1.01 SGD under POL-GEN-03 — part of the trip's charge returned — not the whole contested 4.00 SGD, which no row of POL-RD-24 provides. The rider prefers the amount the rules actually give him to an inflated figure that would fail.

No escalation is warranted under POL-GEN-26: every fact the refund rows need is carried by complete evidence. The disputed value is 4.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final here and the case should be decided, not held.

So this is not row (a) of POL-RD-24, and the within-tolerance no-refund rows (c) and (e) do not apply either. 2. Notification (POL-RD-21). The driver had to inform the rider by in-app chat, or verbally with a call recording, before or at the point of deviation. He did not. The chat log (EV-CHAT-05004) holds only two messages, both about the pickup point and both sent before the trip started (08:35:52 and 08:36:12); the trip record's own derived block shows no messages during the trip and no in-app calls. The rider's reply "Ok" (08:36:12) answers a message about where the car was parked and predates both the trip start and the deviation, so it is not an acknowledgment. The driver's own statement in this dispute — "Forgot to inform, sorry" — concedes the point. This settles the notice limb.

3. Traffic justification (POL-RD-23). The LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-05004-01) reports HEAVY_TRAFFIC on the PIE and its valid window (08:15:42–09:27:22) spans the trip. Whether it sits on the recommended route is left undetermined on the artifact itself, and the policy leaves that question to the adjudicator. It does not need to be resolved here: under POL-RD-24, row (b) (traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km) and row (d) (not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km) both return the excess distance fare. The parties argued this point, and I accept that it makes no difference to the amount.

The excess distance fare is deviation distance × fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge: 1.40 × 0.72 = 1.008, rounded to the cent as 1.01 SGD, which is also the ledger's own derived figure (EV-FARE-05004). The ERP in particular was recorded on the PIE at 08:40:36, before the 08:42:55 deviation, and the recommended route carries the same 1.00 SGD toll, so the reroute added nothing there. The recoverable item on this fare breakdown is 1.01 SGD.

5. Outcome. The rider is owed 1.01 SGD of the 4.00 SGD contested, so under POL-GEN-03 this is a PARTIAL_REFUND of 1.01 SGD, with no driver compensation.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and Driver, this is the decision on TRP-05004 (DSP-05004).

THE DEVIATION IS ESTABLISHED. The platform's own recorded distances are 9.5 km driven against 8.1 km recommended (EV-TRIP-05004), which under POL-RD-22 gives a deviation of 1.40 km. That is 0.40 km beyond the 1.0 km tolerance, so the trip cannot sit in any no-refund, within-tolerance row of the POL-RD-24 matrix. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-05004) shows the route actually taken — leaving the recommended PIE line at the Clementi Avenue 6 exit at 08:42:55 and rejoining at Holland Road / Commonwealth Avenue West at 08:53:16 — which matches the rider's account. The trace is not used to re-measure the distance, per POL-RD-22.

THE DRIVER DID NOT INFORM THE RIDER. POL-RD-21 requires the driver to message the rider before or at the point of deviation. The chat log (EV-CHAT-05004) holds two messages, at 08:35:52 and 08:36:12, both about the pickup point and both sent before the trip started at 08:37:22; the trip record's in-trip message list and its call list are empty, and the log contains nothing after 08:36:12. The rider's 'Ok' at 08:36:12 answers the driver's parking message and was sent six minutes before the deviation, so it is not an acknowledgment and row (a) is not in play. The driver's own statement in this dispute — 'Forgot to inform, sorry' — concedes this limb, and I accept it. Under POL-RD-21 a verbal notice with no recording cannot be established in any event.

THE AMOUNT. Under POL-RD-24 exactly one row applies. The only open question is whether the LTA HEAVY_TRAFFIC advisory (EV-ADVIS-05004-01) is read as intersecting the recommended PIE leg (which would give row (b), traffic-justified but rider not informed) or not (row (d), not traffic-justified). Both rows pay exactly the same thing — the excess distance fare — so the money does not turn on that question and I need not resolve it, and its being open does not escalate the case under POL-GEN-26. The excess distance fare is the deviation distance times the metered per-km rate, without surge: 1.40 km x 0.72 SGD = 1.008 SGD, rounded to the cent as 1.01 SGD. That is the fare ledger's own derived excess_distance_fare_sgd (EV-FARE-05004).

WHY NOT 4.00 SGD. The rider asked for 4.00 SGD. No row of POL-RD-24 provides it: the measure is distance-only and excludes the time fare (3.24 SGD), the base fare (2.80 SGD), the platform fee (0.90 SGD) and the ERP charge (1.00 SGD). The ERP in particular was incurred on the PIE at 08:40:36, two minutes before the deviation, and the recommended route carries the same toll. The rider is therefore owed part of the charge, not the whole contested sum, and not the whole trip fare.

FORUM AND CONFIDENCE. The disputed value is 4.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final here; POL-RD-25's 0.80 confidence bar is met. The artifacts relied on are all assessed COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes, so nothing is impaired and no escalation arises under POL-GEN-26. My confidence is 0.90.

OUTCOME: PARTIAL_REFUND of 1.01 SGD to the rider (the filing party), with no driver compensation. No clause of this version produces a referral on these facts.
